item.title: Quantra - A Superscalar CPU in Turing Complete
item.description:
Quantra is a CPU that I built in the logic simulator Turing Complete.

Features:

  • 32-bit instruction width
  • 16-bit data width
  • 16 GPRs (General Purpose Registers) with 4 write ports and 8 read ports
  • Four 3-stage pipelines capable of executing instructions in parallel
  • Approximately 65KB of RAM (Random Access Memory)
  • Approximately 65KB of persistent SSD (Solid State Drive) storage
  • The ability to load binary data from a file on my computer
  • The ability to execute instructions from memory
  • An ALU (Arithmetic & Logic Unit) capable of performing 10 different calculations
    • AND
    • NAND (Not AND)
    • OR
    • NOR (Not OR)
    • XOR (eXclusive OR)
    • Addition
    • Subtraction
    • Logical Shift Left (LSL)
    • Logical Shift Right (LSR)
    • Compare (Compares two numbers and stores to the flags register)
  • An 80x24 character console screen capable of displaying 8-bit ASCII characters
  • An 160x120 pixel screen
  • A keyboard input to read keystrokes from my physical keyboard
  • A time component capable of reading 64-bit UNIX time in four 16-bit segments

item.title: Documentation of Professor348.github.io
item.description:
This website started as a sort of fun project to see if I could build a site using Hugo that actually looked decent. The inspiration came from Hyacinthe Cartiaux’s website, which I stumbled upon while looking for documentation on some alpha features of the game Turing Complete.

This post’s purpose is to document the development of this website. as a sort of reference for me to look back on, and for other people to gain inspiration from in their own projects. In it, you will find links to all the resources and softwares that I used to build and host this site. In addition, you will find some of the external learning resources that I used throughout the development of this site.
